correctness.rationale: Theorem E of Zeng–Xue–Zeng supplies the infinite forest characterization. The sum-c perfect matching contracts to the simple graph of distances A=c−a and B=c−b on c+1 vertices. Independently, on A+B vertices the two-distance graph is the union of gcd(A,B) cycles, obtained by stepping by A modulo A+B. Deleting the last gcd(A,B) vertices breaks all cycles since each lies in a different residue class, whereas deleting fewer leaves a full cycle. For larger vertex sets the graph still contains the original cycles. This proves the required cutoff and the strict arithmetic inequality. Strict doubling adds only disjoint new edges with fresh endpoints and cannot create a cycle, so the finite forest criterion is sufficient for an infinite support with exactly these first three positions. For gaps x=b−a, y=c−b, the allowable starts satisfy 0≤a≤N−x−y and a<y−gcd(x,y). Without the gcd term, set y=a+1+j and x=1+i; this gives 2a+i+j≤N−2 and leading volume 1/12. The gcd deficit is exact on x+2y≤N+1; outside this triangle the only nonzero deficit is in a strip of width gcd(x,y). Writing x=du,y=dv with d=gcd(x,y), each d gives at most one possible integer u+2v in the strip, yielding O(N²) in total. The main triangle has divisor-sum count Σφ(d)floor((floor((N+1)/d)−1)²/4) and leading term (N²/4)Σ_{d≤N}φ(d)/d², after truncating at d≤N. Möbius inversion gives (6/π²)log N+O(1) for this last sum, verifying the correction and the normalized proportion. Separately, bounded graph and count comparisons covered 969 triples with c≤18 and 22 cutoff values through N=23; these are checks of the finite reductions only.
residual_risks: The checked result counts first-three prefixes across all infinite supports, not three arbitrary occurrences or distinct full words. The inaccessible 2013 theorem passage is not needed to validate the cutoff because of the independent cycle proof.

evidence: Zeng et al. give the general infinite-support forest characterization. The earlier Resultary envelope states that there are at most 1+floor(log₂(N+1)) support positions up to N in a single word, with a Mersenne example attaining the bound. The relevant 2013 paper was not available at theorem level.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A sharp single-word occupancy bound does not count choices of prefixes across many words. The broader forest and Toeplitz criteria are legitimate mathematical inputs, but they provide the pointwise test, not a quantitative estimate on aggregate admissibility.

value.rationale: Passing from a decision criterion for one prefix to the prevalence of extendible prefixes fills a natural counting gap. The limiting one-half density by itself misses an arithmetic bias larger than the usual quadratic counting remainder. Isolating its coefficient separates geometric volume from gcd depletion, a meaningful use of the exact criterion rather than just evaluating small cases.
residual_risks: No higher-prefix counting theorem is inferred.
